Chegg has changed drastically, for the worse. As a STEM student Chegg used to be my go-to for getting solutions in challenging courses like physics and organic chemistry, because the responses were from real-life experts that provided the correct answer ≈98% of the time. Even though AI could be great for broader topics and questions with answers that could involve multiple interpretations, I don’t think the developers realize that it just can’t do science or more complex material at all. That’s the reason most students even use the app, otherwise the question could be typed into chat bots like GPT (with no wait time either). For the price it’s kind of ridiculous that the app has chosen to take this route. They’ve also mentioned in responses to others that you could just downvote the AI-powered response and have the question forwarded to a real person, but there are so many issues with that. First of all there’s no option to initially post the question and have it be blocked from AI answering it. It also adds unnecessary time in waiting for a response because at this point almost every question I post that’s been answered by AI has been wrong, so forwarding it to a real person is inevitable. The majority of students also use Chegg to search up questions that many have already asked, and the AI responses have fully clogged the app to the point where there are so many answers to that one question, most of them answered by AI (who will likely give the exact same answer every time), and most of them incorrect. Usually these responses would have no upvotes or downvotes either, because like I said there’s so many of them, so it’s impossible to tell if it’s the correct answer. If any developers come across this review, please take the criticism and work on restoring the app’s effectiveness and reliability.
